decision: D83: model stateful protocols in Quint before the Lean proofs (#718)
evidenceVocabulary: #718: exhaustive-finite (TLC complete state graph), bounded-no-counterexample (Apalache BMC to maxSteps), sampled (random simulation), witnessed (non-vacuity witnesses), refuted (variant counterexamples), unknown

models.scope: command/perform lifecycle, timers, crash and DO eviction, reconciliation (norn-kernel cell_host.rs; norn-cell host.rs, store.rs)
models.proofLane: K-C binding (idempotency and replay decisions); P9 cell host
implicitStates: I1 enqueued
I2 claimed (volatile Fresh licence)
I3 in flight
I4 request on the wire to the provider
I5 executed at the provider
I6 result recorded
I7 peeked (between peek and commit)
I8 outcome unknown
I9 fenced generation
I10 timer due / fired, incarnation
I11 evicted or crashed
I12 fenced at the provider, refusal not yet committed
assumptions: A1 the provider deduplicates on the operation key (EFFECT-IDENTITY-1)
A2 the provider fences the operation key atomically with its lookup; the cell commits the refusal in a separate step (crash point I12)
A3 a store transaction is atomic, so a crash mid-commit equals a crash before it
A4 DO eviction happens only when idle (assumed, not verified against norn-cell-do)

variants.meaning: without A2's fence, a request still on the wire executes after the cell refused it
a cancelled or replaced timer incarnation fires
dispatch that keeps its volatile licence dispatches a generation twice
a commit that does not mark the generation consumed lets it be consumed again
the consumed generation is missing from consumedGen while the ledger holds it
a commit without the consume fence consumes a generation replaced since the peek

without A1 the provider executes a key once per request: a stale generation's request re-executes the key (execOnce) and can overwrite the outcome before the cell records and consumes the other execution's result (resultFidelity)
without A1, two requests for one operation key both execute

exclusions: EffectRow::Enqueue appending a newer generation of an already consumed command. Under EFFECT-IDENTITY-1 a new business operation carries a new operation key, so the model treats it as a fresh command; reuse of a consumed command id is not modelled.
The restored perform fence (perform_fence_generation): after restore, a reconciled claim is admitted only above the fenced generation; the model reissues from any outcome-unknown state.
FIFO-head claiming: the code claims only the outbox head; the model claims any pending command (an over-approximation).
PARKED-1 out-of-order completion of parked commands.
A4 (eviction only when idle) is an assumption, not verified.

models.scope: fork pin, copy-on-write roots over a content-addressed page store, merge by replay, two-phase reachability GC, export fence (Core 08 Fork lifecycle; #1226 U1/U2, units 3 and 6)
models.proofLane: FORK-ISOLATE (#1226 unit 10): Lean world-indexed non-interference; L1-L6
implicitStates: J1 fork pin with its main horizon
J2 page shared through content-address dedupe
J3 GC between mark and sweep, with its write barrier
J4 promoting, with a durable merge cursor
J5 inherited main label on fork-written rows (pre-U2b)
J6 fork-of-fork receipts minted by a fork below the child's base

variants.meaning: L5: a boundary decision read from the row label lets a fork perform
L3: a dedupe hit during mark/sweep that is not greyed is freed while reachable
L6: the #1226 fence (commit_seq > pin.base.commits) exports a parent fork's records from a fork of a fork
resetting the merge cursor on refusal replays the prefix twice

models.mergeAtomicity: not atomic: commands replay one by one as ordinary main commits (Core 08 FORK-MERGE-1); a refusal keeps the replayed prefix in main and reopens the fork; a later promote resumes at the durable cursor
exclusions: The #1239 finding concerns #1226's head (export_record with the own-base fence). export_record on main has no fork fence at all; re-check there once forks land.

models.scope: per-device stock leases, offline sales, deterministic sync, shortfall and resolution obligations (#1225)
models.proofLane: linear conservation meta-theorem (P6 U5); #1225 design requirements
implicitStates: K1 unsynced fact
K2 fact or ack on the wire
K3 gap awaiting its predecessor
K4 grant in flight
K5 return in flight (sequenced in the device stream)
K6 local deficit after a beyond-lease sale
K7 obligation open, resolved or escalated

variants.meaning: a device that clamps its local balance at zero sells within lease yet creates shortfall
a cell-side reclaim of an offline device's lease turns its within-lease sales into shortfall
a return outside the device's ordered stream races a later sale and drives the lease negative

exclusions: Stranded lease: localTracksLease is one-sided, so the cell can hold lease units for a device that the device can neither sell within lease nor return (lease 1, sell 2 offline, apply, grant 1). Reported on #1225; not prevented by this model.

models.scope: cross-cell commitment: source reserve + outbox, target acceptance with receipt deduplicated by id, reconciliation settled/refused/unknown, query and fence, compensation that can fail (#493 and its design consult)
implicitStates: X1 reserved + outbox pending
X2 command, receipt or query on the wire
X3 accepted at the target, unreceipted at the source (the in-flight claim)
X4 overdue / outcome unknown, with the missed deadline kept
X5 fenced at the target after an unseen-id query
X6 foreign receipt from another cell for the same id
X7 compensation pending or failed
assumptions: B1 each cell commits its side atomically (reserve+enqueue; decide+receipt)
B2 receipts and queries carry the issuing cell, authenticated

variants.meaning: a receipt from another cell settles the commitment
answering an unseen-id query without fencing lets a late command be accepted after the source released, duplicating units
a duplicated command is accepted twice
a target that accepts without its capacity law exceeds it

commands.note: Run on Boat, not the shared host. Traces drop Quint's timestamp/description metadata and record source, step, seed and engine instead.
commands.liveness: quint compile --target tlaplus liveness/<harness>.qnt > <module>.tla; TLC with INIT q_init, NEXT q_step, INVARIANT invariant, PROPERTY live, -deadlock (Apalache.tla and Variants.tla from apalache v0.56.1 on the TLC path)

liveness.engine: TLC 1.8.0 over `quint compile --target tlaplus` output (with Apalache.tla and Variants.tla from apalache v0.56.1)
liveness.method: each harness imports its model, gives faults a finite budget (so 'eventually the faults stop' is explicit and the state space is finite) and states per-action weak fairness; TLC is run on `live` = fairness => properties with the model invariant. TLC finished (complete state graph) only for the cross-cell harness; the cell and offline-leases runs stopped incomplete (results.json: unknown).

harnesses.budget: 1 fault; device 1 sells and returns (2 records), device 2 holds and syncs grants; unit grants, requests, receipts and resolutions; no loss postings
